statement_record.book: In a category E with finite limits (pullbacks + terminal 1), a subobject classifier is an object Ω with a mono true : 1 -> Ω such that every mono m : X >-> Y has a UNIQUE char(m) : Y -> Ω making the square (X -> 1, m, true, char(m)) a pullback; conversely any p : Y -> Ω determines a subobject {Y | p} by pulling true back, and a predicate on Y is a morphism Y -> Ω.
statement_record.intree: Class SubobjectClassifier over `{@Terminal C}` + `{@HasPullbacks C}` with fields Ω, truth : 1 ~> Ω, char m M : x ~> Ω, char_pullback : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one, char_unique : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M; plus classifier_classifies : SubObj x ≅[Sets] (x ~> Ω) with the backward leg sub_reindex h truth_subobject.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — and marginally intree-stronger on two counts: the book ASSUMES true is monic while the library DERIVES it (truth_monic), and the converse direction ({Y | p}) is not merely defined but proved a two-sided bijection with the subobject setoid (classifier_classifies, both round trips). The finite-limit hypothesis matches exactly (terminal + pullbacks). Uniqueness is stated at the level of ≈ on morphisms, the faithful setoid rephrasing of the book's equality. The book's phrase 'a predicate on Y is a morphism Y -> Ω' has no separate in-tree name, but that is a naming convention, not content.

statement_record.intree: For skeletal FINITE sets the construction is literal and computable: FinSet_Classifier has Ω := 2, truth := fin_true, and char m b := fin_of_bool (fin_existsb (fun a => fin_eqb (m a) b)) — 'true exactly on the image' — with char_pullback and char_unique proved (and finset_monic_iff_injective, line 335, giving monos = injections). statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the book's own category: over ALL sets the two-element boolean Ω is not available in-tree (and cannot be, constructively — 'b is in the image of m' is a Type-valued proposition, not a decidable boolean), so the in-tree Sets result is a differently-valued classifier living one universe up, deliberately NOT a `SubobjectClassifier Sets` instance. evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Fun : Category := {| obj := C ⟶ D;  (* objects are functors C ⟶ D *) hom := @Transform C D;  (* morphisms are natural transformations *) id := @nat_id C D; compose := @nat_compose C D; compose_respects := @nat_compose_respects C D |}  — with Notation "[ C , D ]" := (@Fun C D), so Presheaves := [U^op, C] (Theory/Sheaf.v:127)

Class Functor (C D : Category) := { fobj : C → D;  fmap {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : fobj x ~> fobj y;  fmap_respects : ∀ x y, Proper (equiv ==> equiv) (@fmap x y);  fmap_id {x : C} : fmap (@id C x) ≈ id;  fmap_comp {x y z : C} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g }  — instantiated at C^op ⟶ Sets: fobj c is the set of sections over c and fmap f the restriction map, with the two functoriality laws

statement_record.book: For a small category C, a presheaf P on C is a functor P : C^op -> Set; P(c) is the set of sections over c; for f : c' -> c the function P(f) : P(c) -> P(c') is the restriction map, written s|_f; and a morphism of presheaves is by definition a natural transformation.
statement_record.intree: Presheaf U C := U^op ⟶ C and Presheaves := [U^op, C] (Theory/Sheaf.v:124/127) over Construction/Opposite.v's Opposite (line 106); the content is carried by Class Functor (fobj = sections, fmap = restriction, with fmap_id and fmap_comp) and by Fun, whose homs ARE @Transform, the natural transformations, with nat_id/nat_compose making them a category.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with the standard setoid rephrasing: 'Set' is Instance/Sets.v's category of setoids, restriction maps must additionally respect ≈ (fmap_respects), and s|_f is spelled fmap[P] f s. In-tree the notion is more general in two ways — the target category is arbitrary (C-valued presheaves), and smallness of C is not required as a hypothesis, universe polymorphism {o h p} handling the size question instead. The library also carries the dual (Copresheaf U C := U ⟶ C, Theory/Sheaf.v:130), matching the book's footnote.
